idiom_name: blinker named signals (or django.dispatch.Signal) as the process-wide hub
implementation_notes: The hub becomes a module-level registry of named signals instead of an aggregator object: signal('order:placed') returns the same Signal instance everywhere without any code sharing, connect()/connect_via() registers any callable receiver (optionally restricted to one sender and optionally weak, which auto-disconnects unreferenced receivers), and send()/send_async() fan the payload out; the return value collects each receiver's return value as a (receiver, result) pair. Django's dispatch.Signal with the @receiver decorator and send_robust() is the framework equivalent for Django projects. A hand-written hub - a dict mapping event names to lists of weakref.WeakMethod/weakref.ref callbacks - is still justified when the events need instance-scoped channels, typed event objects, ordering guarantees or no third-party dependency; the standard library has no in-process pub/sub.
code_sketch:
from blinker import signal

order_placed = signal('order:placed')           # one shared hub per event name

order_placed.connect(billing.on_order, sender=order_service, weak=True)
order_placed.send(order_service, order_id=42)   # synchronous fan-out, returns results

# without blinker:
# from weakref import WeakMethod
# handlers: dict[str, list[WeakMethod]]  - publish iterates a list(...) copy
pitfalls: send() runs synchronously in the publisher's frame, so a slow receiver blocks the publisher and an exception propagates out of send() unless send_robust() or per-receiver handling is used.
Receivers connected without weak=True keep their targets alive - a bound method in an instance dict is enough to defeat garbage collection and produce a classic listener leak.
The named-signal registry is genuinely global: receivers connected during import or in an earlier test stay connected, so tests need sig.muted() or explicit disconnect().
Signal identity depends on the module-level name registry, which makes two libraries that both define 'order:placed' silently share subscribers.
